documents.t: Algorithmic Security Analysis is an operational screen that contains Securities with Strong, Weak, Potential, and Ambiguous map types assigned by the Security Algorithmic Recon process. The Algorithmic Security Analysis screen lets users manage Security mappings, approve or reject Weak mappings, edit Securities, and rerun an Algorithmic Recon reprocess. It also maintains a backlog and technical data for each Algorithmic Recon process. Date selector: specifies the date range for displaying Securities. Filter set: filters Securities using two filter types (Security Type and Security Code). Operation buttons: the tools for managing Security mappings (Reprocess, Details, Edit Security, Unmap Security, Create Mapping, Approve Mapping, and Reject Mapping). Context menu: options for operating with an individual selected Security. Grid: list of Securities within the time frame specified by the Date selector (1).

The upper toolbar contains the buttons for managing Security mappings. A greyed-out button means the action is unavailable for the selected Security. The available actions are described below. Reprocess button​ The Reprocess button opens the Run Algorithmic Reconciliation dialog, where you run the Security Algorithmic Recon. The Run Algorithmic Reconciliation screen is divided into three sections: General, Tune Algorithm, and Detail Settings. The General section sets the primary Security Algorithmic Recon parameters. Model Type*: type of Algorithmic Recon to reprocess (Security). This option is unavailable and is provided strictly for reference. Definition: dropdown containing Security Reconciliation. Further Algorithmic Recon options will be added as the capability expands. Date: select the date to re-run the Algorithmic Recon for. Override Company: select the Company from the dropdown list to re-run the Algorithmic Recon for. Detail Mode: check the box to enable the Detail Settings section at the bottom of the screen. Owner Definition: check the box to re-run the Algorithmic Recon for all subsidiary Companies and the Owner company afterward. NOTE: If this checkbox is not selected, the Algorithmic Recon will be re-run only for the company selected in the Override Company dropdown (4). Description: brief information about the Algorithmic Recon. The Tune Algorithm section defines the scope of the Security Algorithmic Recon. Matching Strategy Type: select the Recon Strategy for the re-run (Pessimistic or Optimistic). See Principle of Work for details on the Recon Missing Values Strategy. Confidence Level: set the Confidence Level lower threshold. When the Algorithmic Recon is launched in work mode, it rewrites Security entities above the threshold. INFORMATION Algorithmic Recon reprocess can be launched in working or debug mode. Working mode creates mappings, just like the regularly scheduled Algorithmic Recon. Debug mode does not create mappings; instead, it retains the full set of extracted Security entities for Fuzzy learning purposes. The debug mode results are allocated in the Reinforcement Learning matrix. The switch between working mode and debug mode is located in the Detail Settings section. The Detail Settings section specifies the parameters for Detail Mode. NOTE This section becomes available only when the Detail Mode checkbox (5) in the General section is selected. Detail Output Columns After Matching*: the set of columns saved for every compared pair in the reconciliation search space. This field is read-only. It is provided for reference and debugging, so that you can review Pair Similarity and Predicate values during manual analysis. Reinforcement Learning Enabled: switch between working mode and debug mode. Check the box to launch Algorithmic Recon re-run in debug mode. INFORMATION Each Algorithmic Recon run evaluates all possible Security pairs considered by the Algorithmic Security Recon Fuzzy engine. As a result, the best pairs are used to create Security mappings. The remaining candidates in the search space can be reviewed and analyzed on three levels. To review the search space with the calculated Predicates and Pair Similarities, use the Upper toolbar button Details. Details button​ The Details button opens a Mapping Details pop-up screen that shows the right-side Security (Counterparty), the mapped left-side Security (House) and the remaining candidates from the search space that were not mapped. The Mapping Details screen allows users to review Security mappings across three levels and manually change the mapping if the Algorithmic choice was inaccurate. The mapping and candidates are distributed across the following levels: Level 3: all possible mapping variations (in other words, the reconciliation search space). Level 2: best variations selected in all three Predicate groups. Level 1: the actual winner and the mapped Security. Their Security: the right-side Counterparty Security and its basic parameters (Security Code, Security Description, Security Type, and Map Type). Level section: contains mapping candidates grouped into three levels. The number of candidates varies by Security (a Security can have multiple candidates in the Level 3 group or just one, depending on how the Algorithmic mapping performed in that case). Level Up/Level Down: buttons that move you up or down through the levels to review the candidates. Grid: contains the list of mapping candidates and shows their technical reconciliation background data (calculated Similarities and Predicates values). Context menu: the actions you can run against the selected mapping. CONTEXT MENU Context menu of the Mapping Details screen contains various options that depend on the mapping itself and its strength. Possible options are reviewed below. Unmap: available for established Strong mappings. Use it to break the Security mapping. When the mapping is broken, the Security is added to the Not Mapped Securities grid. Change Mapping to this Security: available for Potential candidates that were not mapped to the Security. Use it to manually establish the mapping. The previous mapping is automatically broken. Approve or Reject Mapping: available for established Weak mappings. Use it to approve or decline the mapping. Rejected mappings are added to Rejected Mappings. INFORMATION Using the Level Up and Level Down buttons, users can jump between groups to review the Similarity parameters and each Predicate that constitute the Pair Similarity value. The Level grid provides full technical details for every mapping candidate in the search space. You can select the required columns in the Column Chooser: By default, only the most important Predicates are stored in the database and are visible on the Mapping Details screen. However, if the Algorithmic Recon is re-run in debug mode, additional values will populate the Level grid. Important The search group candidates are not stored in the database permanently because this would add load to the servers and slow down the application. The entities are cleaned up one month after the reconciliation process. When the entities are purged, the Level grid displays the message: Edit Security button​ Edit Security button opens the Security Editor (Reference Data Security Master tool). It is used to edit Security instruments and manage their mapping lists: Basic Security information: displays the Security Code, Security Description, and Type. Tab bar: an operational ribbon with Security tabs. The tabs may vary depending on the Security type. General section: contains the primary Security parameters. Identifiers: contains Security identifier parameters. Issuer: contains Security issuer parameters. Save and Close/Save/Cancel: use these buttons to save your changes or discard them. SECURITY MAPPINGS Mappings tab displays all mappings assigned to the Security, including those created by Classic and Algorithmic Recons, the Reference Data Job, and manual mapping. Each accounting and banking system may label the same Security differently. For example, the client’s accounting system may store it as MSFT, while a bank system stores it as MSFT US (based on BBG ID). Another bank may report it as MSFT.O, and another counterparty may label it as MSFT SHS. As a result, House Securities typically have multiple mappings. You can create manual mappings directly in the Mappings grid: Unmap Security button​ Unmap Security button breaks an existing active mapping. When an Algorithmic active mapping is broken (it can be Strong, Weak or Potential), the mapping is considered erroneous. When this happens, the mapping’s initial parameters (Security Id Left + Security Code Right + Security Map Type Right) are added to the blacklist and will no longer appear in the Algorithmic Recon search space. Unmapping also adjusts the matrix table on the Reinforcement Learning screen. Before breaking a mapping, users must confirm the action in the pop-up window: NOTE If a mapping is broken by mistake and later restored, the statistics revert as if the break never happened, returning to the status quo. Create Mapping button​ Create Mapping allows you to create a mapping manually. It opens the Mapping Details screen with the candidates selected for the Security’s mapping search space. When you create a manual mapping, the system updates mapping statistics and adjusts the Reinforcement Learning matrix table accordingly. If you try to create a mapping for a Security that is already mapped, the following warning appears: Approve Mapping/Reject Mapping buttons​ Approve Mapping and Reject Mapping buttons are used for Securities with a Weak or Potential Algorithmic Map Type. A Weak mapping has a decent Confidence Level, but it is not high enough to qualify as Strong; therefore, it requires approval from an authorized user. NOTE When a mapping is rejected, it is automatically added to the Rejected Mappings list (available on the screen of the same name). A rejected mapping severely impacts the algorithmic reconciliation routine.

The Algorithmic Security Analysis grid contains Algorithmic Security mappings’ parameters. The primary columns of the grid are: Algorithmic Map Type: indicates mapping certainty (Strong, Weak, Potential, Ambiguous). Is Active: indicates whether the mapping is active (applies to the Security). Is Approve Required: indicates whether the mapping requires approval. Has Ambiguity Mappings: indicates whether the Security has ambiguous mappings. You can filter entities in the grid by selecting a Strength value in the Algorithmic Map Type column. NOTE Securities in the grid are color-coded so users can quickly review their status. The color codes are: Not mapped Security: the available action is Create mapping. Mapped Security: the available action is Unmap Security. Security needs approval: the available actions are Approve mapping and Reject mapping.

Security Mappings is the primary Security Recon screen. It aggregates all Security mappings and mapping suggestions that persist in the system (created by both Classic and Algorithmic recon, Reference Data Job, Hub Client, or established manually by users). Date selector: specifies the time range for displaying Security mappings. Show Mappings: selects the mapping status used to filter Security mappings in the grid (All, Active, Approve Required, Ambiguous, Potential). Operational buttons: actions that can be executed against mappings in the grid. Grid: lists all Security mappings for the selected time period. Context menu: actions available for the selected item in the grid. INFORMATION The Approve Required, Ambiguous, and Potential statuses refer to mappings established via Algorithmic Recon. Each status implies a possible action against the Security. As a result, the Mapping Details screen and its available tools vary by status. See the examples below. Mapping statuses (Approve Required, Ambiguous, Potential)​ Approve Required mapping status implies the following Mapping Details screen and available options: Their Security: the right-side Security (delivered from the Counterparty source) with basic parameters. Candidates: list of House Securities that make up the candidate list. Context menu for the main candidate: allows users to Approve or Reject the mapping. The main candidate is highlighted in yellow. Context menu for other candidates: allows users to map the right-side Security to a different candidate. If this happens, the main candidate is automatically rejected, and the suggested mapping moves to the Rejected Mappings. Search Notes: text block containing brief logs about the suggested mapping search and results. If Search Notes are blank, it means the system purged the logs after one month. Advanced View: select to switch to the Levels grid and review the mapping’s technical details. INFORMATION The Advanced View button takes users to the Level grid with the full candidate list and technical reconciliation parameters (Predicate variables and Pair Similarities). The Levels grid supports the same actions (Approve, Reject, and Map to this Security). Ambiguous mapping status implies the following Mapping Details screen and available options: Their Security: the right-side Security (delivered from the Counterparty source), with basic parameters. Levels: list of candidates grouped by algorithmic mapping level. Context menu for all candidates: allows you to create a mapping to the selected Security. Other mapping candidates remain on lower levels and are not rejected. Pair Similarity of the candidates: calculated Pair Similarities for the candidates. INFORMATION Ambiguous status is assigned when the Confidence Level is identical for two or more candidates. In this case, the algorithm cannot determine the correct mapping and delegates the decision to the user. Once the correct candidate is identified, it can be mapped manually. Potential mapping status implies the following Mapping Details screen and available options: Their Security: right-side Security (delivered from the Counterparty source) with basic parameters. Levels: list of candidates grouped by algorithmic mapping level. Context menu for all candidates: allows you to create a mapping to the selected Security. Other candidates remain on the lower levels but are not rejected. INFORMATION Potential mapping status is assigned to a Security when the combination of Confidence Level and Distance places the mapping in the gray zone of the Reinforcement Learning matrix table. This means the candidate list is formed, but the top-scoring candidate is not strong enough to be mapped automatically. Potential mappings can be rejected (unmapped). In this case, the mapping is considered erroneous. When this happens, the mapping’s initial parameters Security Id Left + Security Code Right + Security Map Type Right are added to the blacklist and will never enter the Algorithmic Recon search space.

Operational buttons are used to manage Security mappings and handle mapping requests originating from the Security screen. Request Data: press to load entities into the grid when filters are set (Date range and Mapping status). Automatic loading is turned off by default. Details: opens the Mapping Details screen. The user interface depends on the Security’s mapping status. Edit Security: opens the Edit Security screen, which mirrors the Security Master Editor. It allows you to modify all Security parameters, including mappings. Create Mapping: press to create a Security mapping with the top Confidence Level-scoring candidate. This option is available only for mappings in Potential. Approve Mapping: press to approve a Security mapping in Approve Required status. Reject Mapping: press to decline a Security mapping in Approve Required status. Unmap Security: press to break an existing Security mapping.

Reinforcement Learning is an operational analytics screen that consolidates and analyzes Algorithmic Recon data in a specialized matrix table. It recalculates the accuracy of previously created mappings and generates a heatmap of accuracy zones for Algorithmic Recon mappings. For details, refer to the Principle of Work section. Date selector: selects the time range for Reinforcement Learning statistics. Distance rows: Distance value ranges. Quality parameters: sub-rows showing quality parameters (Total verified, Verified as correct, Unverified). Confidence Level columns: Confidence Level value ranges. Totals: totals per Quality Parameter group for each Distance row. Summary: averages for Strong, Weak, and Unused mappings, including Accuracy and Coverage for each group. INFORMATION The Reinforcement Learning screen is scheduled to run once per day at the end of the day for the previous business day. During the run, Reinforcement Learning recalculates Confidence Levels and Distances for all mappings (including approved and rejected mappings), gathers statistics, and regenerates the accuracy zones in the matrix table. To do this, Algorithmic Recon runs for the past date using real historical input and produces new outputs for mappings and mapping suggestions. These outputs are then compared with existing real mappings (Etalon mappings): verified, approved, rejected, corrected, or manually created. FUZZY ENGINE SELF-LEARNING PROCESS By comparing the calculated outputs of an Algorithmic Recon run with Etalon mappings, the Fuzzy engine can self-learn and evolve. This learning process enables the engine to calculate actual accuracy for each Confidence Level/Distance segment and apply a similar expected accuracy rate to future mappings within the same segment. Segments are divided into three groups: Strong (matrix green cells): accuracy is higher than 99.5%. Weak (matrix yellow cells): accuracy is between 98% and 99.5% (that is, at most one error per hundred mappings). Potential (matrix white cells): accuracy is less than 98%. As a result, the Reinforcement Learning matrix table dynamically adjusts the heatmap accuracy zones based on automatic Strong mappings, approvals and rejections of Weak mappings, and manual mappings created by users. NOTE Due to the dynamic nature of the Reinforcement Learning matrix table, the number of columns and rows (and the chunk ranges) change automatically and are not controlled by the user. The matrix table skeleton is calculated based on the average distribution of mapping volume (each row and column includes the nearest number of mappings). Important The Reinforcement Learning matrix begins to work only after the system accumulates a significant number of verified matching instances. This threshold is set individually for each client during implementation (the default value is 10,000 matching instances). Additionally, the accuracy zones shift in response to users breaking mappings. For example, the Strong cell for a Confidence Level of 89–93 with a Distance of 1–30 can be downgraded to Weak or Potential if a user manually breaks a Strong mapping they deem incorrect within this cell.

Matrix table shows the accuracy zones of Strong, Weak, and Potential Map Types for Security mappings. Rows represent Distance ranges, and columns represent Confidence Level ranges. Each cell contains three quality parameters: Total verified: number of legitimate mappings (constituted from correct and rejected mappings). Verified as correct: number of mappings that were verified (constituted from approved mappings, manually created mappings, or mappings created by Classic Recon). Unverified: number of mappings that are not currently verified (constituted from mappings that require approval and have not yet been approved). Each value lets users drill down to the list of mappings within that Distance and Confidence Level segment. When a value is clicked, the user is directed to the Learning Details grid. Summary​ Summary is an overview at the bottom of the Reinforcement Learning matrix table. It shows the totals for Total verified, Verified as correct, and Unverified mappings across all three groups (Strong, Weak, and Unused). It also displays each group’s Accuracy and Coverage: Accuracy: calculated as the total number of suggested mappings verified as correct divided by the total number of suggested verified mappings. Coverage: calculated as the total number of suggested Broker Security-to-House Security mappings divided by the total number of not-mapped Broker Securities.

Learning Details is an overlay screen that displays all mappings within the selected matrix-table cell and quality parameter. To open the Learning Details grid, click a value in the matrix table on the Reinforcement Learning screen: Model Id: currently not used filter. Confidence From/To: specify the Confidence Level range to filter Securities in the grid. Default values are taken from the selected cell on the matrix table. Distance From/To: specify the Distance range to filter Securities in the grid. Default values are taken from the cell of selected value on the matrix table. Grid: Security mappings displayed based on the selected filters. Context menu: selective options that can be performed against the Security mapping.

Context menu adapts to the parameters of the Security mapping. The available options and the conditions for using them are listed below. Unmap Security The option is available for Security mapping where the mapping is Fuzzy Mapped and is not rejected. When applied to the mapping, it switches to the Is Rejected status: Restore Mapping The option is available for Security mappings in the Rejected state. When applied, it restores the mapping to its previous status: Reject The option is available for Security mappings where the mapping is Fuzzy Mapped and is not rejected. When applied, the mapping switches to the Rejected state, and the combination of Security Id Left + Security Code Right + Security Map Type Right will not enter the Algorithmic Recon search space going forward: Create The option is available for Security mappings where Etalon Security Id is not specified and the mapping is not rejected. When applied, a new mapping is created with the combination Security Id Left + Security Code Right + Security Map Type Right: Change Mapping to Security Id Left The option is available for Security mappings where the mapping is not Fuzzy-correct, Etalon Security Id does not match Security Id Left, and the mapping is not rejected. When applied, the mapping is changed to the Security Id from the left side: INFORMATION Two options are always available: Details (opens the Mapping Details screen with the mapping candidates grouped by level) and Edit Security (opens the Security Master Editor to adjust Security parameters and mappings).
The Not Mapped Securities and Rejected Mappings screens are aggregation grids for, respectively, Securities that did not find a match and Security mappings that were rejected by users.

The Not Mapped Securities grid contains Securities extracted from incoming feed files that were not included in any Positions’ search spaces for the Algorithmic reconciliation process. As a result, reconciliation was not performed because there were zero mapping candidates. Date To: select the date for which to display not mapped Securities. Reprocess: press the button to open the Algorithmic Recon Reprocess screen and initiate the reprocess procedure. Grid: list of not mapped Securities for the selected day. Context menu: contains the Details option that opens the Mapping Details pop-up screen.

The Rejected Mappings grid contains Security mappings from the Weak certainty group that users rejected on the Security Analysis screen. Grid: list of mappings in the Rejected state. Context menu: contains the Restore Mapping option, which returns the mapping to its previous state. Important Rejected mappings directly impact the Algorithmic reconciliation processes. Before starting, the Fuzzy algorithm checks the pool of rejected mappings; if it finds a mapping flagged as Rejected, it excludes entities with the same Security Code, Map Type, and Company ID from the search space.

Format Step-by-step instructional guide covering the full setup and operation of the Approver mobile application. Target Readers Transaction Manager module users, including treasury operations managers, collateral management officers, fund controllers, and credit operations specialists. Description Enables users to review, approve, or reject transactions on the go. Walks users through initial configuration, authentication, and day-to-day operations. Supports a critical routine: time-sensitive Transaction requests are verified without delay. Business Impact Closes a critical operational gap in Transaction management: the ability to approve or reject on the go. Essential when managing asset movements under credit or collateral agreements, where delays carry significant financial and contractual risk.

The Approver Mobile Application (Approver) lets users review and manage Vouchers on the go. Approver runs on smartphones and tablets and is available for iOS™ and Android™ devices. It can be installed from the App Store™ and Google Play™. NOTE To add an extra layer of security and prevent unauthorized access, Approver cannot connect to the environment without administrator approval. To connect your device to the system, complete the following steps: License & Device Approval.

Device Enrollment is the process of connecting your personal handheld device to the platform. To enroll your device and start using it, complete the following steps: Licensing Installation & First launch Device Approval
The Approver Mobile App license is a paid item, and licensing requires an update to your contract. Contact your sales manager to discuss the available options.

Download and install the Approver Mobile App from the App Store™ or Google Play™. The app supports the current versions of iOS™ and Android™. IMPORTANT: The Mobile App will not work on rooted (jailbroken) devices.

When you open Approver for the first time, you must configure the connection to your environment. Only then will your device appear on the Device Approval screen. During the initial launch, you will be prompted to allow push notifications on your device: If accepted: notifications will be sent directly to your device. Notifications may also include confirmation codes required for voucher approval. If declined: notifications will not be displayed. Confirmation codes will be delivered via email. When you open the Approver for the first time, specify the following parameters to connect to your environment: Access Code: a unique identifier for your tenant (company). INFORMATION: Contact your representative to obtain the Access Code for your company’s users. This code is confidential and should be shared only with authorized users. Login and Password: enter the credentials for your user profile. About: tap to view information about the Approver application. *The Approver application does not support single sign-on (SSO); therefore, the password you use to log in must be your system password. After you authorize with the Access Code and your credentials, the device registration process begins. An administrator must approve your handheld device to complete the process.

Your mobile device must be approved before the Approver can connect to the environment. When your credentials are accepted during the initial launch, your device appears on the Device Approval screen (System Administration module > User Administration folder > Device Approval screen). The Device Approval screen is an administrative console used to manage mobile device enrollment. It is available only to administrators: Upper toolbar: contains Approve, Reject, and Set notification options. Device Code: a unique code assigned to each device associated with the application. Approval State: the approval status. Only Approved devices can read data in Approver. Push/Email Notifications: shows how the device receives notifications (including confirmation codes). INFORMATION If you need to disconnect the device from the system, select the device on the grid and click the Reject button. The device will be automatically disconnected from the system, and the user will be forcefully logged out of the Approver. Any repeated login attempt will be unsuccessful. To change the notification delivery method, click the upper toolbar button Set notification options. The Device Notification Options screen opens with two checkboxes (as shown below). Select the preferred method and click Save. The change will apply to the mobile device. Once the device is successfully approved on the server side, the application displays a Confirmation screen prompting you to enter the confirmation code sent to you either as a push notification or to your registered email address. Enter the code in the Confirmation Code field, then click the Next button. You will then be taken to the Access Code screen, where you must set up a short PIN code for Approver login:

You can configure the length of the Access Code used for Approver login and the number of login attempts allowed for the application user. Use the following Company Preferences to set up these parameters: Mobile Device Pin Length: specify a 4-, 6-, or 8-digit PIN as a User Preference Value. If the PIN length is set to 8 digits, users must create an 8-digit PIN. Mobile Device Login Attempts: the number of login attempts is configurable. A value of 3 means users have three attempts to enter the PIN code. After three unsuccessful attempts, the user will be logged out of the application and will have to enter the Access Code, Username and Password. The Approver login screen shows a countdown indicating how many login attempts remain: TIP You can also log in using your fingerprint or Face ID if your device supports it. The corresponding prompt will appear on the Approver login page when you set up the PIN code. NETWORK OR SERVER ISSUES If the Approver displays an error when you attempt to log in, perform the following troubleshooting steps: Verify that your username and password are correct. Check the internet connectivity on your handheld device. Enable Airplane Mode, wait 30 seconds, then disable it. If no issues are detected on your side, contact the Support Team for immediate assistance. The Approver always warns customers about maintenance work performed on the servers.

documents.t: The primary purpose of the Approver application is to allow users to review and approve or decline Vouchers remotely. The My Approvals screen displays a list of all Vouchers in the system that are ready for an approval or rejection decision. Vouchers are automatically sorted by Voucher ID, with the most recent Voucher at the top. The Approver user interface contains the following items: Left menu: provides options to review Vouchers in different states. Here you can also change the application theme (Dark & Light), select custom statuses, and switch your tenant. Search: an advanced search engine that allows you to filter Vouchers by date range, date type (e.g., Settlement Date), sort by (e.g., Voucher Id desc), and status. The results are displayed on the All Vouchers screen. Voucher details: a short recap of the Voucher details (total amount size, total number of Transactions that constitute the Voucher, State, Attachments, etc.)

Approver allows users in the parent tenant (Company) to switch tenants in a multi-tenant environment and then review and manage Vouchers for child tenants. To change tenants, open the left menu and tap the Company name. A list of available tenants appears. Tap the tenant you want to switch to. NOTE You must have access to the parent tenant to switch to a child tenant. When you are logged in to a child tenant, you will not be able to see any other tenants except your own.

The Approver application includes an advanced search engine that lets you filter Vouchers by Voucher ID, date range, date type, and status, and sort results in the desired order. After you set the search parameters, results are displayed on the All Vouchers screen. Simple search example: a user needs to find a specific Voucher by Voucher ID. They enter the Voucher ID in the Search data field and adjust the date range. Advanced search example: a user needs to review all Vouchers with the Awaiting Approval status, starting with those with the largest amounts. They specify the date range, Voucher status, and Sort order.

Vouchers are listed on the My Approvals screen, which opens as the default start page. To review a Voucher’s contents and details, tap a Voucher to open the Voucher Details screen: Voucher recap: shows the Voucher’s State, Currency, Amount, and Settlement Date. Notes: tap to open the Notes screen with Internal and External Notes of the Voucher. Outputs: tap to open the Outputs screen, where you can download the generated Voucher’s output messages. Advanced: tap to open the screen with Audit data and Attachments. Wires: list of the Wires that constitute the Voucher. Tap on the Wire to open the Wire’s Details screen. Approve/Reject: buttons you use to approve or reject the Voucher. INFORMATION You can control whether users can download output messages and attached files using the Mobile Device File Download Option (no spaces) Company Preference: This preference supports four values: None: attachments and output messages are unavailable for download on the handheld device. Attachments: users can download only attachments clipped to the Vouchers. Outputs: users can download only the Vouchers’ output messages. AttachmentsAndOutputs: users can download both Attachments and Outputs. Notes​ The Notes section contains internal notes (for users) and external notes (for external users). It is displayed only if internal or external notes were added during Voucher submission. You can select Notes text by tapping and holding your finger on the screen. Outputs​ The Outputs section contains output messages in XML format (UTF-8 encoding). You can download them and review transfer details before the transfer is sent to the receiving party. NOTE: If no outputs are generated for a Voucher, this section is not displayed. Advanced​ The Advanced section contains additional Voucher information: Audit (logs that show all actions applied to the Voucher and its contents) and Attachments (files such as confirmation letters, agreements, and invoices that are attached to the Voucher and can be downloaded to your device). TIP For security reasons, follow general safety policies and remove any downloaded attachments from your handheld device after approving or declining the Voucher. Wires​ Vouchers consist of one or more Wires. To review a Wire, tap it to open a detailed recap: General section: contains Settlement Date, Currency, and Type. From/To: shows the sender’s and receiver’s Portfolio, Account, and the Amount of transferred money. Notes: contains Internal and External notes created for this Wire. Advanced: contains Audit, Attachments, and SSI/DI. Cancel: tap to cancel this Wire. NOTE: This action must be approved. Refer to Approval confirmation.

Approval or Rejection of a Voucher is a mandatory step in the Voucher Workflow. Depending on the workflow configuration, a Voucher may require multiple approvals before it is delivered to the operational institute. Users with delegated approval permissions can approve or reject a Voucher in the Approver application. Approver offers three ways to approve or reject a Voucher: Directly from the Voucher: open the Voucher Details screen and tap one of the buttons at the bottom of the screen. Bulk Approval/Rejection: select multiple Vouchers on the All Vouchers screen (tap and hold any Voucher to activate the Select All checkbox), then approve or reject your selection using the buttons at the bottom of the screen. The number of selected Vouchers is not limited. Swiping Right/Left: on the All Vouchers screen, place your finger on a Voucher and swipe (right to approve or left to reject). After swiping, tap Approve or Reject to complete the action.

Approval confirmation is mandatory for approve, reject, or cancel actions. The confirmation code is delivered to your device based on the selected notification delivery method (push or email). The action is completed only after you enter the confirmation code in the corresponding field. You must enter a supplementary note before you can confirm the Voucher for approval or rejection.

Reject for Edit is an option available within the Reject action. It assigns the Voucher the Rejected for Edit status, allowing you to update the Voucher details and resubmit it. To reject for edit, tap Reject on the Voucher screen to open the Confirmation screen. Then select the Reject for Edit checkbox, add a comment, and tap Submit reject:

You can lock a Voucher to prevent other users from editing it. To lock the Voucher, tap the unlocked lock icon in the top-right corner of the Voucher interface. A locked Voucher can be unlocked only by the user who locked it or by users with permission to unlock Vouchers. To unlock the Voucher, tap the locked lock icon: Vouchers with a Failed or Rejected status cannot be locked. To complete the lock/unlock action, you must confirm it with the code delivered to your device based on the selected notification delivery method (push or email):

Format Getting Started guide introducing key features of the GL Manager screen, supplemented with real business use cases. Target Readers Fund accountants, general ledger accountants, financial controllers, and NAV reporting specialists. Description Onboarding article for the GL Manager screen within the Transaction Manager module. Helps new and existing users orient quickly within the interface and understand common practices. Business Impact Brings full transparency to ledger records within a unified system — a single point of visibility across accounting data. Allows accountants, analysts, and operations staff to immediately identify discrepancies in their own or counterparty records and react in real time.

documents.t: GL (General Ledger) entries are ledger records produced from Transactions and Vouchers for clients’ accounting systems. GENERAL LEDGER ENTRIES Accounting systems typically use double-entry bookkeeping, where each Transaction is represented by two cash flow movements—a debit and a credit—that affect different accounting categories. These categories are defined in the Chart of Accounts (CoA), which may include multiple hierarchical levels. The CoA example is presented below. Category Bank Account GL Account Description Transaction Types Assets Account A 10556 Cash Account A Income Expense - 10557 General Investments Buy Sell Liabilities Account B 10558 Loan Account B Drawdown Paydown - 10559 Distributions Loan Allocation Capital Call Any Voucher or Transaction that represents an actual money movement can contain multiple General Ledger entries required for downstream accounting systems. GL entries are produced according to GL allocation rules—system and/or custom. GL Allocation Rules define the General Ledger entry templates applied to the target Transactions.

GL entries are created and edited in the Voucher Details screen. For each Voucher or Transaction that must be reported to the accounting system, create or update the GL entries on the General Ledger Entries tab. Once created, they automatically populate the aggregating grid in the GL Manager screen. General Ledger entries tab: go to this tab to create and manage GL entries for the transactions. Operational bar: contains buttons to create (Add), modify (Edit), save, cancel, automatically generate GL entries (Generate Entries), and preview the GL entry output (Preview Output). Grid: lists the GL entries created for this voucher. Details: GL entry parameters section. You can modify these parameters after switching the entry to Edit mode. It contains the following parameters: Transaction*: select the transaction within the voucher for which you want to create the GL entry. This field is mandatory and is automatically populated if the voucher contains only one transaction. If the voucher contains more than one transaction, you must specify it manually. Description: provide a brief description for the GL entry. By default, this field is populated with the transaction’s External notes (if specified) or Internal notes. Chart of Accounts parameters*: select the parameters of the GL hierarchy. All parameters are created, managed, and customized in the Dictionary tool (path: Reference Data module > Preference folder > Dictionaries screen). Effective Date*: select the date when the GL entry can be included in the ledger books. This field is mandatory. NOTE: By default, the Effective Date repeats the Settlement Date of the selected transaction but can be changed manually. Credit/Debit*: choose the direction of the asset movement. This field is mandatory. INFORMATION: In accounting systems, a Credit GL entry for one account must be paired with a Debit GL entry for another account, and vice versa. When GL entries are generated automatically, these credit/debit entries are created automatically. Currency*: select the GL entry currency. By default, the transaction’s currency is filled in automatically. This field is mandatory. Amount*: enter the transaction amount related to the GL entry. This field is mandatory. Allocation Rule: select the allocation rule from the dropdown. This parameter’s values are created and managed in the Dictionary tool. Reference and External Reference: provide the GL entry with reference numbers. By default, the Reference number is taken from the transaction. INFORMATION The Details section of the GL Allocation Rule may also contain UDFs (User Defined Fields), if they were implemented for the environment. CHART OF ACCOUNTS PARAMETERS The Details section of a GL Entry includes Chart of Accounts parameters that define the customizable GL hierarchy. These parameters help categorize General Ledger Entries and add specificity. You can customize these parameters in the Dictionary tool in the Reference Data module (Reference Data module > Preference folder > Dictionaries screen). Chart of Accounts parameters are displayed across three levels (Level 1, Level 2, Level 3), with GL Type and GL Account Level grouped by level. Each GL Type can be linked to a parent parameter. For example, if the General Expenses parameter has a parent Account Level parameter BBHY-1, selecting the GL Transaction Type in the Details section automatically populates the remaining parameters (in this case, Account, Group, and Class). If you modify captions for Account-level parameters, the corresponding field names in the Details section of the General Ledger Entries tab will also change. INFORMATION You can control how many Chart of Accounts parameters are shown in the Details section of the Allocation Rule Editor by using the Company Preference General Ledger Available Account Levels. This preference can be set to 1, 2, or 3, and it defines how many Chart of Accounts parameters are displayed in the Details section:
User Defined Fields for the GL entries are bespoke fields tailored for every individual client during system implementation. UDFs can capture any required additional information.

The Operational bar on the General Ledger entries tab lets you add, edit, save, and remove GL entries for the voucher. It also includes two special buttons that enhance the tab’s capabilities: Generate Entries: click to have the system automatically create all GL entries according to the GL Allocation Rule that targets the voucher. Preview Output: click to generate and download the preview output file based on the GL Message Layout. The file contains all created GL entries and their parameters—a snapshot of the output that will be delivered to the accounting system. INFORMATION The system includes a default system GL Allocation Rule that produces either two or four records (depending on the number of accounts that participate in the transaction). For every account, the system automatically creates Credit and Debit entries and populates Details parameters with the transaction details (Amount, Currency, Date, Notes). You can create an unlimited number of custom GL Allocation Rules to produce GL Entries of your own design. GL Message Layout​ GL Message Layout defines the GL output file that contains all generated GL entries and is delivered from the system to the client’s endpoint. The default GL Message Layout is shipped with the system and includes pre-designed markup. You can modify the output file markup here: Reference Data module > Message Layouts folder > Message Layouts screen. Find the Message Layout with the GL Output Message Type parameter and switch it to Edit mode: NOTE You can modify certain parameters (Output format, File Name, File Extension) and redesign the output message markup (click the Edit in Designer button to open the DevExpress designer). ExampleGeneral Ledger entries The voucher contains a single transaction with a settlement date of 7/23/2023: a simple cash wire transfer for $555,000: The user, Author Curry, must create the corresponding GL entries that will be posted and delivered to Aqua Trading’s in-house accounting system when the transaction is settled. They use the Generate Entries button to create all GL entries automatically: four entries—two for each account involved in the transfer (Credit and Debit): To verify the integrity of the GL entry output before it is delivered to the accounting system, Author Curry generates the preview, downloads it, and confirms that the output message follows the Message Layout markup they established. Once the General Ledger entries are created for the Transaction, they automatically populate a special GL Manager grid that is developed specifically for aggregating GL Entries:

GL Allocation Rule is a Reference Data item that defines how to generate GL entries for a selected set of Transactions. The GL Allocation Rules grid is located here: Reference Data module > Cash/Wires folder > GL Allocation Rules screen. The GL Allocation Rules screen displays a grid that contains all existing GL Allocation Rules in the system, both default and custom: Upper toolbar: a set of buttons used to create (Add), modify (Edit), duplicate (Copy), and remove (Delete) GL Allocation Rules. You can also Export Rules as JSON configuration files and Import them into new environments. Grid: a list of all GL Allocation Rule configurations in the system. INFORMATION The system can contain an unlimited number of GL Allocation Rules. Rule priority is determined by the Order parameter you define in the GL Allocation Rule Editor. Note that no user can modify or remove the default system GL Allocation Rule. Its priority is generally the lowest.

GL Allocation Editor is the tool for building rules. Use the Add or Edit buttons on the upper toolbar to open the editor in a pop-up window. The GL Allocation Rule Editor includes the following parameters: Code*: specify the code for the GL Allocation Rule. No spaces are allowed. This parameter is mandatory. Name*: specify the name of the GL Allocation Rule. This parameter is mandatory. Order*: enter the priority number that determines when the GL Allocation Rule is applied. The order is ascending: 1 is the highest priority, 2 is lower than 1, 3 is lower than 2, and so on. This parameter is mandatory. NOTE: If a Transaction matches the conditions of multiple rules, the rule with the highest priority is applied. Active: select this checkbox to activate the rule. Inactive rules are not applied to Transactions. Description: provide a brief description of the rule. Matching Rule*: build the matching rule that determines which Transactions the rule targets. In the screenshot above, the clause includes Transactions with amounts between 100 and 150 USD. Advanced Mapping Mode: select this checkbox to enable the Mapping Expression field, where you can write the expression manually. Clear it to return to the Mapping Templates grid. Mapping Templates grid: lists the rule’s templates and their parameters. Template parameters: select a template from the grid and define the parameters and their sources. Mapping Templates​ Mapping Templates section defines how many GL entries will be generated for the target Transaction, and which parameters will be used. The section also includes UDFs, if they are configured for the environment: INFORMATION In custom GL Allocation Rules, you can control the number of GL entries produced and their parameters. For example, the Mapping Template in the screenshot above produces only two GL entries for the Credit and Debit sides. Optimizer is a module that generates data-driven recommendations to help optimize client portfolios for improved profitability and risk management. The Optimizer engine consists of specialized algorithms (Algos), each developed to address a specific functional objective. These Algos analyze client data within the platform and generate recommended actions (Suggested Actions). The Optimizer engine processes client data (including rates, balances, currencies, interest rates, and maturity dates) and generates Suggested Actions based on predefined algorithmic logic: Standard Data Source: provides the Optimizer engine with the system data used by the triggered Solution. Optimizer pulls data from the sources designated in the Algos that make up the Solution. Solution: processes the source data and runs Algos one by one, in the order specified in the Solution setup. For example, an Algo can suggest closing negative balances with high interest rates by moving funds to the account with the lowest rate within a portfolio. Below is an example of this Algo: foreach (var portfolioId in OptimizerCustodianAccountBalances.Select(a => a.PortfolioId) .Distinct().ToList()) { var accounts = OptimizerCustodianAccountBalances .Where(a => a.RequiredDebit < 0 && a.IsCurrencyBalance && a.CurrencyId == a.PortfolioCurrencyId && a.PortfolioId == portfolioId); var bestDebitRateCustodianAccount = accounts.OrderBy(a => a.DebitRate).FirstOrDefault(); if (bestDebitRateCustodianAccount == null) continue; foreach (var debitAccount in accounts.Where(a => a.DebitRate > bestDebitRateCustodianAccount.DebitRate && Math.Abs(a.RequiredDebit) >= bestDebitRateCustodianAccount.WireThreshold)) { await Transfer(bestDebitRateCustodianAccount, debitAccount, Math.Abs(debitAccount.RequiredDebit)); } }
